Coverage objects

Source: R/coverage.R
coverage.Rd

package_coverage(), file_coverage(), code_coverage(), function_coverage() and environment_coverage() return a coverage object, which records how many times each part of the code was executed.

Working with coverage objects

Rather than using the list directly, you will usually want to:

  • Get a data frame with one row for each expression with as.data.frame() (as.data.frame.coverage()), or one row for each line or function with tally_coverage().

  • Get the overall percentage with percent_coverage(), or the percentage for each file with coverage_to_list().

  • Find the lines or functions which were never run with zero_coverage().

  • Get the execution counts as a named numeric vector with value().

  • Browse the coverage with report() or file_report().

Structure

A coverage object is a named list with one element for each traced expression of R code and each line of compiled code. Each element is a list with:

  • value: the number of times the expression or line was executed.

  • srcref: a srcref with its location. Its srcfile attribute holds the name and lines of the source file.

  • functions: the name of the function containing it, or NA for compiled code.

  • tests: only present with options(covr.record_tests = TRUE), see covr.record_tests.

The names of the elements are the base name of the file followed by the eight numbers of the srcref, separated by :. For example foo.R:10:3:12:4:3:4:10:12 is an expression from line 10 column 3 to line 12 column 4 of foo.R (see as.data.frame.coverage() for the meaning of each number). The srcfile of the srcref, or the filename column of as.data.frame(), gives the path of the file.

Coverage objects from package_coverage() also have the attributes package (information about the package, such as its package name and path), root (the directory file names are relative to, or NULL) and, if clean = FALSE, library (the install_path).

With options(covr.record_tests = TRUE), coverage objects also have a tests attribute with the test calls, see covr.record_tests.

Examples

cov <- code_coverage("add <- function(x, y) { x + y }", "add(1, 2)")
cov
#> Coverage: 100.00%
#> /tmp/RtmpvWYfuG/source.R186f3a984b82: 100.00%
as.data.frame(cov)
#>                               filename functions first_line first_byte
#> 1 /tmp/RtmpvWYfuG/source.R186f3a984b82       add          1         25
#>   last_line last_byte first_column last_column first_parsed last_parsed value
#> 1         1        29           25          29            1           1     1
names(cov)
#> [1] "source.R186f3a984b82:1:25:1:29:25:29:1:1"
cov[[1]]$value
#> [1] 1
